newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan criticises Israeli construction in E.Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Annan criticises Israeli construction in E.Jerusalem.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Thursday criticised Israel's decision to build homes for Jews in East Jerusalem and said any action that impeded future peace negotiations was unhelpful.
"The secretary-general has learned with concern of the decision of the government of Israel to proceed with the construction at Har Homa," U.N. spokesman Juan Carlos Brandt said.

"He considers unhelpful any action which may impede the final status negotiations scheduled to begin next month between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation," the statement said, referring to talks on difficult unresolved issues.
"No objective is more important than for the parties to find mutually agreeable solutions to the sensitive issues involved, including Jerusalem," the spokesman added.
The statement was prompted by the decision of an Israeli ministerial committee on Wednesday authorising construction of 6,500 homes on a pine-covered ridge between Jerusalem and Bethlehem.
The hill, called Har Homa by Israel and Jabal Abu Ghneim by the Palestinians, was captured by Israel from Jordan during the 1967 Middle East war.
Annan, visiting London before leaving for Paris, held a previously-scheduled meeting on Thursday with Israeli President Ezer Weizman, currently on a state visit to Britain.
"The question of the settlements was discussed, as well as the question of (U.N.) reform and relations between the United Nations and the state of Israel," Brandt said.
